paper: Albuquerque et al. 2021, Marine Drugs 19:621 (DOI 10.3390/md19110621, PMID 34822492)

open_questions.q: Do the atratumycin-like NRPS proteins in MA3_2.13 BGC region_008 actually encode a novel atratumycin congener, or are they a divergent orphan that would fail to produce the depsipeptide skeleton under any known culture condition?
open_questions.basis: Paper reports 49-57% amino acid identity between MA3_2.13 NRPS proteins in BGC #8 and the reference atratumycin NRPSs; our replication confirmed the cluster-level MIBiG hit (BGC0001975, blast score 24833) but did NOT run per-protein BLAST or heterologous expression. Atratumycin (Sun et al. 2018) is a lipodepsipeptide with anti-mycobacterial activity from S. atratus, and 49-57% identity is on the edge where domain architecture might be preserved while adenylation-domain substrate specificity has drifted enough to load a different amino acid. Without either LC-MS metabolomics of MA3_2.13 cultures or CRISPR activation of the silent cluster, the 'novel congener' claim is a bioinformatic inference.
next_steps: Run per-gene BLASTp of MA3_2.13 region_008 NRPS ORFs against the atratumycin BGC0001975 reference proteins to reproduce the paper's 49-57% identity numbers.
Predict A-domain substrate specificity with NRPSPredictor2 / SANDPUMA and compare with atratumycin's known amino acid loading order.
Culture MA3_2.13 under a small OSMAC panel (Fe-limited, high-salinity, sponge-mimic media) and run untargeted LC-HRMS/MS with GNPS analog search seeded on atratumycin (m/z ~1300 Da region).
If metabolomics is negative, consider promoter-refactoring the pathway-specific regulator identified in region_008 for heterologous expression in S. coelicolor M1152.

open_questions.q: Is the taxonomic placement of MA3_2.13 as a genuinely novel Streptomyces species (subsequently named S. profundus) robust to the addition of the 200+ Streptomyces type-strain genomes deposited to NCBI/GTDB since the paper's 2021 MLSA cutoff?
open_questions.basis: The paper's novel-species claim rests on whole-genome ANI < ~78% to its closest reference (SCSIO 3032) and MLSA distance to a 2021-vintage set of type strains; our replication confirmed the ANI-distance conclusion (skani rejected, fastANI 80.85%) but used the same paper-selected reference set. Streptomyces is one of the most rapidly-expanding bacterial genera in public databases; GTDB r220 (2024) added many marine and deep-sea Streptomyces genomes that were not in the paper's 2021 comparison. A closer relative may exist now that would demote MA3_2.13 from 'novel species' to 'novel strain of an existing species' or refine its position in the S. albiflaviniger / S. griseus / S. sanglieri neighbourhood.
next_steps: Run skani search against the full GTDB r220 Streptomyces representative set (~800 genomes) for MA3_2.13 and record the top 5 hits with ANI + aligned fraction.
Rerun MiGA (http://microbial-genomes.org) with the current type-material database and record the p-value for novel-species assignment.
If any post-2021 genome falls in the 95-96% ANI band, run a targeted MLSA (atpD, gyrB, recA, rpoB, trpB) tree limited to that clade to test whether MA3_2.13 still sits outside all named species.
Cross-check the formal S. profundus species description (post-2021 taxonomic literature) for phenotypic and chemotaxonomic evidence beyond genomics.

open_questions.q: Does the antiSMASH v5 -> v6 count drop from 32 to 27 BGCs for MA3_2.13 reflect the merging of true co-located sub-clusters into single regions, or does some fraction represent v6 correctly discarding v5 false-positive BGC calls?
open_questions.basis: Our replication reports MA3_2.13 = 27 BGCs (v6.1.1) vs paper's 32 (v5.0). We attribute this to v6's stricter co-location and detector rules that merge closely-spaced protoclusters, and note category composition is preserved. However, we did NOT run v5.0 side-by-side to prove the drop is purely mechanistic merging. Some of the missing 5 BGCs could be v5.0 calls that v6 discards outright (e.g. v5 was known to over-call certain terpene / other-KS false positives that later rule-refinement removed). If so, the paper's 32-BGC number is a slight over-count and the 23.1%-of-chromosome BGC-density claim would need small downward revision.
next_steps: Rerun antiSMASH v5.0.0 (the paper's version) on GCF_020740535.1 inside a pinned docker image and compare region-by-region against our v6.1.1 output.
Classify each v5-only region as (a) merged into a v6 super-region, (b) split from what v6 calls a single region, or (c) genuinely dropped by v6 detector-rule changes.
For any category-(c) regions, cross-check with GECCO (a machine-learning BGC predictor with different failure modes) to see whether the v5 call is supported by an orthogonal method.
Recompute the '23.1% of chromosome is BGCs' number under both v5 and v6 and report the range rather than a single value.

open_questions.q: Does S07_1.15's classification as S. xinghaiensis (ANI 95.83% ANIb in paper; 96.66% skani / 96.12% fastANI in our rerun) reflect true conspecificity, or is S07_1.15 a novel sister lineage sitting right at the ~95% ANI species boundary where the deep-sea Madeira population has diverged from the type strain?
open_questions.basis: S07 vs S. xinghaiensis S187 (GCA_000220705.1) sits right on the 95-96% ANI species-boundary knife-edge (Jain et al. 2018). The paper called this conspecific; we confirmed with two modern methods (both above 96%) but the aligned fraction was not reported in our summary table, and species-boundary calls at 95-96% ANI are known to be sensitive to k-mer method biases and to reference-strain quality. S. xinghaiensis was originally described from marine sediment (Zhao et al. 2009 IJSEM), and Madeira Archipelago populations may represent a geographically-isolated deep-sea variant.
next_steps: Compute alignment-fraction (AF) alongside ANI --- true conspecificity requires AF > 60-70% at 95-96% ANI; low AF suggests genomic reduction / niche specialisation.
Run PYANI-ANIb (the paper's exact algorithm) to directly reproduce the 95.83% number and reduce method-choice ambiguity.

Include additional S. xinghaiensis-clade genomes (any GenBank Streptomyces with >95% ANI to S187) in a whole-genome tree to see whether S07_1.15 groups inside the S. xinghaiensis clade or sits as an outlier sister lineage.
Compare S07_1.15's 24 BGCs to the S. xinghaiensis S187 BGC repertoire --- large BGC-content divergence at ~96% ANI would argue for population-level niche differentiation.

open_questions.q: Given the paper's claim that MA3_2.13 is RiPP-poor and PKS-rich while S07_1.15 is RiPP-rich with zero type-I PKS, does this represent a genuine ecological / niche-differentiation signal between sediment-dwelling and sponge-associated deep-sea Streptomyces, or is it a two-genome sampling artifact?
open_questions.basis: The paper draws a biosynthetic contrast between the two isolates as if it were a phenotype of their respective niches (500-1500 m sediment vs coral-associated sponge). Our replication confirmed the compositional contrast (zero T1PKS in S07_1.15 is exact) but the sample size is n=2 --- one genome per niche. The RiPP-rich / PKS-rich dichotomy could easily be a species-level trait (S. xinghaiensis vs S. profundus lineage) that has nothing to do with sediment-vs-sponge ecology. Without additional genomes from the same two niches, the ecological interpretation is under-supported.
next_steps: Query IMG/M and MGnify for additional Streptomyces MAGs / isolate genomes from (a) deep-sea marine sediments and (b) marine sponge holobionts; count how many sit inside the S. profundus vs S. xinghaiensis clades.
Rerun antiSMASH on 5-10 additional genomes per niche and test whether the RiPP-vs-T1PKS balance segregates by niche or by phylogeny (PGLS / phylANOVA controlling for the species tree).
Cross-reference with the culture-independent BGC surveys of Paoli et al. (Nature 2022, Tara Oceans SMAGs) for niche-conditional BGC-composition priors.

If the ecological signal survives phylogenetic correction, follow up with in-situ metabolomics (e.g. sponge tissue extraction with GNPS matching to atratumycin / triacsins analogs) to test whether the predicted chemistry is actually produced in the sponge niche.
